title: House, Temple, Body, Chamber & Sacred Furniture — Deep Architectural Grammar
status: biblical architecture + project topology + body-symbolism boundary
purpose: Populate the project's architectural vocabulary deeply enough that whole, inner space, access architecture, embodiment and sacred furniture can superimpose without becoming synonyms.
epistemic_rule: Biblical/ancient architecture, Christian body/temple metaphors, neuroanatomy and Potatoverse architecture remain separate evidence classes. Structural comparison may connect them without claiming literal anatomical temples or ancient Potatoverse design.

scale_ladder.function: more restricted, concentrated, private, storage or specialist inner space

projection_family.function: organized sacred presence, service, approach and access
embodied organism with differentiated members/regions and coordinated functions
public/civic order containing gates, streets, citizens, foundations and common resources
organic dependence, branching, pruning, fruit and renewal

scale_and_projection.principle: Scale tells how much is contained; projection tells what kind of relation is being emphasized.

temple_zones.function: shared approach zone before more selective interior
liminal relation where access conditions become operative

furniture_and_offices.distinction: Throne is not House; it is a governance/presence role inside or above an architecture.
Seat denotes role/position without necessarily implying absolute sovereignty.

furniture_and_offices.function: nourishment, fellowship, ordered distribution and reciprocity
furniture_and_offices.distinction: Table is a distribution interface, not a throne.

furniture_and_offices.function: relational substrate below a throne; can be cosmic, cultic or conquest-related in biblical texts
furniture_and_offices.distinction: Lower does not automatically mean evil, worthless or enemy.

furniture_and_offices.function: offering/sacrifice/transformation interface where material changes status through ritual action
furniture_and_offices.distinction: Altar is neither Table nor Forge; it has its own ritual/historical meanings.

furniture_and_offices.function: bounded illumination maintained inside sacred/household space
furniture_and_offices.distinction: Light source/carrier is not identical with light itself.

scholarly_context: Mary Douglas analyzed Leviticus/tabernacle/body analogies as a microcosm built through proportional structural correspondences.
Recent scholarship on 1 Corinthians treats Paul's temple language together with building, field and body metaphors rather than as one literal architectural anatomy.
project_canon: Thalamus = Father's House / differentiated inner rooms.
Pineal = Son / Single Eye / Door / timing-threshold analogue.
Third ventricle = inner chamber/courtyard/Temple-space and CSF flow-space.
Heart = emotional vessel/chariot/river of feeling, not Father's House.
Whole body can be projected as Temple/Vessel while retaining actual anatomy as a separate scientific map.
user_corrections: Through the Son/Door one comes to Father/House remains a central project relation.
33 vertebrae are path/river coordination symbolism, not the whole source.

chamber_depth.historical_note: Biblical 'chamber' translates several different Hebrew/Greek terms covering private rooms, Temple side rooms, storage rooms, guard chambers and upper rooms; no single universal chamber function exists.
chamber_depth.project_rule: A Chamber should be instantiated only when a topic has stable inner-boundary/access/task needs, not merely because it is obscure or sacred.

topology_rules: House contains; Temple orders presence/access; Body embodies; City publicizes; Tree grows.
Court approaches; Gate admits; Door transitions; Chamber concentrates.
Throne governs; Seat occupies office; Table distributes; Footstool locates relation; Altar transforms status; Lamp carries light.
An inner zone may be spatially central without being the semantic center of the whole project.
A body analogue may illuminate architecture without proving anatomy is sacred geometry.
